A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SceneMI, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplements support reliable comparison. Existing supplementary material can be matched despite its relocation after the references in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on clean and noisy TRUMANS and real-world GIMO, alongside ablations, runtime measurements, and video reconstruction examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds repeated-seed results in Table 9 and qualitative demonstrations and failure cases in Figures 8–10.

M1.justification: The scene encoders, denoiser, losses, keyframe imputation, noise-handling schedule, and video reconstruction procedure remain unchanged. Section 9.2 supplies COINS-generated poses through the existing keyframe interface; no revision to SceneMI's algorithm is documented.

E1.justification: TRUMANS, GIMO, and PROX remain the dataset coverage. Sections 9.2 and 9.4 add qualitative testing with semantically generated keyframes and rare narrow-passage interactions, modestly extending the evaluated input and interaction scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MDM, StableMoFusion, SceneDiffuser, Wang et al., OmniControl, and CondMDI. Tables 3, 4, and 7 retain MDM, OmniControl, and CondMDI. COINS supplies keyframes in the new demonstration and is not evaluated as a competing method.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the reported TRUMANS test fraction from 20% to 10%. Section 9.3 adds a four-second interval test using only endpoint keyframes. These are limited protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish whether the split revision reflects rerunning experiments or correcting documentation.

E4.justification: The existing scene/noise ablations, keyframe-selection analysis, and hyperparameter studies are retained. Sections 9.2–9.4 add semantic-keyframe integration, a longer endpoint interval example, and illustrated failures involving narrow passages and noisy or complex scene geometry.

E5.justification: v1 reports runtime uncertainty in Table 7 but no analogous uncertainty for its main motion-quality results. Section 9.1 and Table 9 newly report 20 random-seed runs with means and 95% confidence intervals for four metrics in the clean and noisy TRUMANS settings, substantially expanding statistical reporting. Independent retraining across those seeds is not specified.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained. Table 9 adds aggregate results, including clean-setting jerk of 0.193 and collision ratio of 0.114, and noisy-setting collision ratio of 0.109. Figures 8–10 add qualitative successes and failures. These are additional findings rather than replacements of the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and diffusion losses in Section 3 and geometric optimization equations in Section 8 are retained. No new or substantively revised definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: scene-aware motion in-betweening, dual scene descriptors, handling noisy keyframes, real-world generalization, and monocular-video HSI reconstruction. The supplementary additions support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 9.1 interprets the repeated-seed results as evidence of stability. Section 9.4 adds specific limitations involving motions rarely seen during training and spatial constraints missed in complex or noisy scene geometry. These supplement the unchanged limitations in Section 5.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies that synthetic noise excludes the start and end frames; this is additional preprocessing documentation, without establishing a historical implementation change. Section 9.2 identifies COINS as the source of generated keyframes. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, baseline adaptations, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations to SnapMoGen and two Hwang et al. 2025 works on goal-driven motion synthesis and flexible keyjoint control. Section 9.2 demonstrates compatibility with the already cited COINS. The overall research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 moves the supplement after the references, adds its title and Section 9, introduces acknowledgements, adjusts affiliation and internship wording, and repairs the unresolved table cross-reference in Section 4.1.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 and Figures 8–10. Existing supplementary tables and Figures 6–7 are relocated with the supplement, while the main displays retain their content with limited spacing, scaling, and page-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: Table 9 improves evidence about stochastic stability, while the concrete failure cases in Section 9.4 clarify the limits of generalization. The preprocessing clarification and additional demonstrations provide smaller benefits. These gains are limited: the original benchmark scores remain unchanged, and the unexplained test-fraction revision from 20% to 10% leaves uncertainty about the settings behind those retained scores.
